chapter: Learning from players; Jonah Jones lessons
title: Louie Metcalf and Ed Swayzee
summary: Maxwell talks about Calloway's trumpet players and the solo on My Weakness.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Trumpeters I admired: rating the horn players

blocks.x: If it's possible, I'd like to just throw a couple of trumpet player's names at you, not to eulogize or say anything about them, either you knew them or some people along the line. You feel like that?
Yeah, I'm very indiscreet. I'll make a remark.

Not being a trumpet player but being around and listening to a lot of jazz, I've found in listening to it that a great deal of names we all know, like the General, everybody knows Louis Armstrong and Dizzy, Charlie Shavers, Clifford Brown and you can just name on, the cats during the day. Clark Terry and Chuck Magione, and I don't know whether they'd want their names mentioned in the same order or not.
But I came along in an era, since I'm a few years older than you -- I wondered did you ever hear or know anything about Louie Metcalfe?
Yeah, I'd heard but I don't know too much about him.
Well, he was one of the trumpet players, he played -- did some work at (unintelligible)
Well, some of the trumpet players from that time, there was a fellow with Calloway named Ed Sways that I --

No, but he wrote a tune called 'My Weakness' and he played a solo on that that is one of the most beautiful solos I ever heard. There were two trumpet solos, one was muted followed by the open solo. I'm told the open solo was Ed Swayzee, and I asked Doc Cheatham if the muted solo was him, and he says he thinks it was.
Probably was. Doc Cheatham was in the band long before I was.
Yeah, a great player at that time. And I thought he was great.
I was not in the band with Swayzee. He was out -- died or something before --
Killed in an automobile wreck, yeah.
Yeah, he was out of the band before I came in, but I heard the records. I have the records here, and it's lovely.
